title: Binary search
objective: Find an item in a sorted array by halving the part that is still in play.

sources.title: Cormen, Leiserson, Rivest and Stein, Introduction to Algorithms, 4th ed. (MIT Press, 2022): binary search
Sedgewick and Wayne, Algorithms, 4th ed.: section 1.1, BinarySearch

simplifies: All values are distinct here. With repeated values you often want the first or last match, which needs a small change: keep going after a match instead of returning.

quiz.prompt: About how many checks does binary search need for 1,000,000 sorted items?

options.explanation: Right. Each check halves the range, and 2^20 is about a million.
That would be square-root steps. Halving is far faster.
That is half the list: a linear search's average, not binary search.

quiz.prompt: What does binary search need from its input?

options.explanation: Right. Sorting is what lets one comparison rule out half.
Size doesn't matter: it shines on huge arrays.

options.text: The target must be in it
options.explanation: It also tells you, quickly, when the target is missing.
